common_mistakes: Starting the exterior door replacement before Historic District / BAR approval is issued — Charleston can stop the job if the exterior change is done first
Assuming same-size door replacement is exempt because the opening is not changing — exterior envelope work still needs a permit in this historic district context
Submitting a modern replacement door that does not match the approved historic profile, lite pattern, material, or finish
Failing to verify whether the existing frame, sill, or trim repair crosses into structural or water-resistive barrier work that could expand the permit scope

pro_tips: Bring a photo of the existing front elevation and the proposed door cut sheet to the historic reviewer — it speeds up BAR review on exterior changes
If you are matching the existing opening exactly, keep the manufacturer spec sheet showing no size change, because that helps the reviewer and inspector see it is a like-for-like replacement
Charleston is strict on exterior historic details; getting BAR signoff before you order the door can save you from a costly re-order
Use the city permit office phone number before submitting if the property is in a local historic overlay and you are unsure whether the door is a repair or alteration
